questions.question: What is an LLM fundamentally trained to do?
options: Look up answers in a live database
Predict the next token given the preceding text
Translate text into a fixed internal language
questions.explanation: LLMs generate output one token at a time by predicting the next token from everything before it.

questions.question: A team notices that Hindi customer emails cost more to process than English ones of similar length. What is the most likely reason?
options: The model charges a surcharge for non-English languages
Hindi emails are always longer in word count
The context window is smaller for Indic languages
Indic scripts usually break into more tokens per word than English
questions.explanation: Pricing is per token, and Indic scripts typically tokenize less efficiently than English, so the same content uses more tokens.

questions.question: Why can the same prompt produce different answers on different runs?
options: The model samples from a probability distribution over next tokens
The model's training data changes between runs
The model deliberately avoids repeating itself across users
questions.explanation: At each step the model samples from possible next tokens, so outputs vary; clear instructions, examples and fixed formats reduce this.

questions.question: You need a model to cite the source for a company's revenue figure. What is the most reliable approach?
options: Ask it to cite sources from memory
Raise the temperature so it searches harder
Provide the relevant document and ask it to quote the sentence it used
Ask the question in capital letters so it is more careful
questions.explanation: Without documents a model may invent plausible references; supplying the source and asking for a quote grounds the answer.
